bib.title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2019 (33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can a harder successor to GLUE, with more diverse task formats and human baselines, keep measuring progress in general-purpose language understanding once GLUE is saturated by pretrained models?
hypothesis: Significant progress on SuperGLUE should require substantive innovations in sample-efficient, transfer, multitask, and unsupervised or self-supervised learning, since BERT-based systems still lag humans by nearly 20 points.
contributions: Eight harder NLU tasks selected from an open call for proposals by BERT and human baselines
More diverse task formats (coreference, QA) beyond sentence and sentence-pair classification
Human performance estimates for all tasks
Revised leaderboard usage rules and credit assignment

method.summary: Eight tasks (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) plus two diagnostics (AXb broad-coverage entailment, AXg Winogender) are scored by an equal-weight average over tasks. Baselines are most-frequent-class, CBOW (GloVe), bert-large-cased fine-tuned per task, and BERT++ with intermediate MultiNLI/SWAG fine-tuning; human performance is estimated with Mechanical Turk majority votes.
method.task: general-purpose language understanding benchmark (QA, NLI, WSD, coreference)

models.name: BERT (bert-large-cased)
models.architecture: BERT large, cased; simplest possible head per task, separate fine-tuned copy per task

models.name: BERT++
models.architecture: BERT with STILTs-style intermediate fine-tuning: MultiNLI for CB, RTE, BoolQ; SWAG for COPA

other.heads: [CLS] + logistic regression for BoolQ, CB, RTE, WiC (WiC also concatenates marked word representation); scalar projection for COPA; per-answer logistic regression for MultiRC; per-candidate probability for ReCoRD; self-attention span pooling + logistic regression for WSC

metrics.name: SuperGLUE Avg
metrics.definition: equal-weight mean of task scores; multi-metric tasks first averaged over their metrics

metrics.name: Gender parity score (AXg)
metrics.definition: percentage of Winogender minimal pairs with the same prediction

metrics.name: MCC (AXb)
metrics.definition: Matthews correlation on collapsed two-class diagnostic

eval.protocol: Test set via private-label leaderboard, max two submissions per day and six per month. Human estimates: MTurk workers, training phase up to 30 dev examples, qualification at median performance and at least 5 HITs, then 100 random test examples per task (full test set for WSC), 5 annotators each, majority vote; $23.75/hr average pay. Human numbers for WiC, MultiRC, RTE, ReCoRD taken from prior papers. Single run reported; no seeds or variance stated.

results.claim: BERT++ test-set average on SuperGLUE trails the estimated human average by nearly 20 points.
results.setup: Test sets, BERT++ vs Human (est.), Table 3
results.table: Table 3, row BERT++ vs Human (est.), column Avg (71.5 vs 89.8)

results.claim: Fine-tuned BERT raises the SuperGLUE average by about 25 points over the trivial baselines.
results.table: Table 3, row BERT, column Avg (69.0; Most Frequent 47.1, CBoW 44.3)

results.claim: Largest human-machine gap is on WSC; BERT scores below simple baselines there.
results.setup: Gap between best baseline and human on WSC test
results.quote: The largest gap is on WSC, with a 35 point difference between the best model and human performance.

results.claim: Intermediate MultiNLI training gives 2-5 point gains on CB, RTE and BoolQ; SWAG gives about 8 on COPA.
results.quote: Using SWAG as a transfer task for COPA sees an 8 point improvement.

results.claim: GLUE state of the art (88.4) exceeded estimated non-expert human performance (87.1) by 1.3 points, motivating SuperGLUE.
results.setup: GLUE as of early July 2019, XLNet ensemble
results.quote: the current state of the art GLUE Score as of early July 2019 (88.4 from Yang et al., 2019) surpasses human performance (87.1 from Nangia and Bowman, 2019) by 1.3 points

results.claim: Models obtain near-perfect gender parity on Winogender only because accuracy is near chance.
results.table: Table 3, row BERT, column AXg Acc. (97.8 / 51.7)

results.claim: Human accuracy on the collapsed broad-coverage diagnostic is 88% (MCC 0.77); BERT++ reaches MCC 38.0.
results.quote: We estimate an accuracy of 88% and a Matthew’s correlation coefficient (MCC, the two-class variant of the R3 metric used in GLUE) of 0.77.

results.claim: BERT++ dev average is 74.6 versus BERT 72.2.
Excluded tasks: BERT beat the crowd human baseline on PAWS-Wiki (91.9 vs 84% accuracy) and Quora Insincere (67.2 vs 66.7 F1).
results.quote: For PAWS-Wiki, we report that BERT achieves an accuracy of 91.9%, while our human baseline achieved 84% accuracy.

results.claim: Nearly half the tasks have fewer than 1k training examples and all but one have fewer than 10k.
results.quote: with nearly half the tasks having fewer than 1k examples and all but one of the tasks having fewer than 10k examples

limits: Baselines are single-run BERT-large only; no seeds, variance, batch size, schedule or hardware given.

Human baselines are conservative, from crowd workers with brief instructions (authors concede this); human numbers for four tasks come from other papers and WSC/MultiRC etc. use different test subsets.
Winogender offers only positive predictive value; does not cover non-binary or gender-neutral pronouns.
MultiRC Outside Best is evaluated on a subset of the test set.
Dated: benchmark was saturated by later models (not stated in this paper); authors expected the gaps to be hard to close.
